As I lurker myself , I don't necessary like the 20 CCP policy. I do, however, think it's a smart move. Voat is in its infancy and needs content. Requiring people to comment fuels that content. With that said, it will be interesting to see whether they get rid of the 20 CCP threshold once the community grows to a larger size.

I think it was implemented to encourage the community to become more involved. When I first created a reddit account, I largely lurked and only commented twice in an entire year, and those were on smaller subreddits and little more than a line. Voat seems to want to encourage its users to take part in the conversation and the community and be more active as a whole. /v/introduction is set up to welcome new users, and hopefully get them on their way to that 20 CCP threshold, which should (in theory) only be easier as the community grows. My biggest concern, as a counterpoint to to the growing community = reaching the CCP thresholds is as the community grows, many people's comments will be buried with those on top getting the most. I am torn on whether new users will find it easier or harder.

I like the idea behind the requirement; it encourages discussion and community building. However, as someone who, on Reddit, posted once in a blue moon when I had a good piece of content or something good to contribute, the upvoat rule is kind of ridiculous.

I think it needs modified. As is, 100 CCP to downvote does encourage people to get involved early, as well as making votebots and brigading slightly harder. But it really hurts lurkers, who may take months to get up to 100 CCP.

I think it would be more useful to lower the requirement, but apply it on a per-subverse basis. For instance, to downvote in /v/movies, you would need 25 CCP from comments made in /v/movies. This wouldn't hurt the lurkers very much, while still encouraging participation. But the biggest positive is effectively stopping vote brigades before they can even start.

With this method, if you want to vote brigade from one sub to another, every person brigading would need to have already been active and constructive in the sub they are attacking. While you could possibly get a large number of people upvoating each other to do this, that takes a larger level of coordination that more brigades completely lack.

I think it's great. It really isn't hard to get up to 20 CCP, and it makes a lot more sense for the downvoat limit to be even higher. If you're not waiting until you have 100 CCP to start downvoating things chances are you don't really get the culture yet and would just mess it up (I know I would). I'm torn on lurkers here... I mean you should kind of have to contribute to things in order to shape which things are rewarded with voats (on a significant scale. Everyone can still voat to a certain extent.)
